name: Melech
overview: Melech is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, noted in Scripture as the son of Micah. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. This places him within the genealogical records that trace the lineage of the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Melech is a proper name meaning 'king' in Hebrew. It is not indicated that this name was given by God, but its meaning reflects a royal title common in the biblical context. The name itself stands as a straightforward identifier without additional titles or divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Melech is the son of Micah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text concerning Melech.
scriptureSignificance: Melech's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin, as preserved in 1 Chronicles 8:35. Such genealogies are important for understanding the continuity of God's people and the fulfillment of His promises through tribal lines. Though Melech himself is not highlighted for specific deeds or roles, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage of His chosen people.
